questions.knowledge_point: Computing the Image of a Line Given by an Equation in Slope-Intercept Form
questions.problem:
Consider the line $y=-2x+3$ and linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

What is the equation of the image of the line under the action of $T?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that the line $y=-2x+3$ passes through the points $U(0,3)$ and $V(1,1)$ since the coordinates of both points satisfy the equation.

To find the image of $U$ and $V$ under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing the coordinates of the points:

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & -2 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective image points are ${U}^{′}(-6,-3)$ and ${V}^{′}(-2,2).$

Finally, we write the equation of the line that passes through ${U}^{′}$ and ${V}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}}(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-(-3) & =\frac{2-(-3)}{-2-(-6)}(x-(-6)) \\ y+3 & =\frac{5}{4}(x+6) \\ 4y+12 & =5x+30 \\ 5x-4y+18 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the line $y=4x-1$ and linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -3 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

What is the equation of the image of the line under the action of $T?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that the line $y=4x-1$ passes through the points $Q(0,-1)$ and $R(1,3)$ since the coordinates of both points satisfy the equation.

To find the image of $Q$ and $R$ under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing the coordinates of the points:

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -3 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -10 \\ -2 & 6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective image points are ${Q}^{′}(3,-2)$ and ${R}^{′}(-10,6).$

Finally, we write the equation of the line that passes through ${Q}^{′}$ and ${R}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}}(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-(-2) & =\frac{6-(-2)}{-10-3}(x-3) \\ y+2 & =-\frac{8}{13}(x-3) \\ 13y+26 & =-8x+24 \\ 8x+13y+2 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the line $y=2x+1$ and linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

In **standard form**, the equation of the image of the line under the action of $T$ is

{{field-1}}$=-3.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that the line $y=2x+1$ passes through the points $A(0,1)$ and $B(1,3)$ since the coordinates of both points satisfy the equation.

To find the image of $A$ and $B$ under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing the coordinates of the points:

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 7 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective image points are ${A}^{′}(2,-1)$ and ${B}^{′}(7,-2).$

Now, we write the equation of the line that passes through ${A}^{′}$ and ${B}^{′}$ in point-slope form:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}}(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y+1 & =\frac{-2+1}{7-2}(x-2) \\ y+1 & =-\frac{1}{5}(x-2)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we transform the equation of the line to standard form:

$$
\begin{aligned}y+1 & =-\frac{1}{5}(x-2) \\ 5y+5 & =-x+2 \\ x+5y & =-3\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the line $y=3$ and linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

In **standard form**, the equation of the image of the line under the action of $T$ is

{{field-1}}$=21.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that the line $y=3$ passes through the points $P(0,3)$ and $Q(1,3)$ since the coordinates of both points satisfy the equation.

To find the image of $P$ and $Q$ under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing the coordinates of the points:

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 3 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 3 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}9 & 10 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective image points are ${P}^{′}(9,3)$ and ${Q}^{′}(10,1).$

Now, we write the equation of the line that passes through ${P}^{′}$ and ${Q}^{′}$ in point-slope form:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}}(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-3 & =\frac{1-3}{10-9}(x-9) \\ y-3 & =-2(x-9)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we transform the equation of the line to standard form:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-3 & =-2x+18 \\ 2x+y & =21\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the line $-4x+y+1=0$ and linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

In **standard form**, the equation of the image of the line under the action of $T$ is

{{field-1}}$=6.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that the line $-4x+y+1=0$ passes through the points $P(0,-1)$ and $Q(1,3)$ since the coordinates of both points satisfy the equation.

To find the image of $P$ and $Q$ under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing the coordinates of the points:

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 6 \\ -2 & 6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective image points are ${P}^{′}(-1,-2)$ and ${Q}^{′}(6,6).$

Now, we write the equation of the line that passes through ${P}^{′}$ and ${Q}^{′}$ in point-slope form:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}}(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y+2 & =\frac{6-(-2)}{6-(-1)}(x+1) \\ y+2 & =\frac{8}{7}(x+1)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we transform the equation of the line to standard form:

$$
\begin{aligned}7y+14 & =8x+8 \\ 8x-7y & =6\end{aligned}
$$

$$
8x-7y=6
$$
